messages:
zara: quick heads-up — flipped the fp8 kernel on a tiny canary (H100 + L40S) for orion-7B shadow run. ran our 2k prompt eval. seeing a consistent quality regression on long-prefix flows, rouge-L down ~2.4 pts and ppl up ~3%.

mohit: can you paste the exact canary id and commit? baseline numbers?

zara: canary id cny-2024-07-16-12, kernel commit 1f9b2e. baseline fp16->current fp8 kernel. latency p50 improved ~12%, p90 ~9%. but quality delta on longprefix subset is the issue.

ash: (thumbs) — wait who is oncall for kernel?

ash: typo — meant @ashley :)

ashley: looking. grabbed the eval artifacts from s3://redwood-evals/cny-2024-07-16-12. quick summary:

```
subset       baseline_fp16   fp8_kernel    delta_quality   p50(ms)   p90(ms)
short       0.812           0.811         -0.1pts         45        78
longprefix  0.734           0.710         -2.4pts         52        89
perp        12.3            12.7          +3.3%           45        89
```

ashley: gfx: latency wins, but longprefix degredation concentrated on sequences with warmup tokens >512 and repetition rate high.

eva: my hunch is kv-cache tiling + accumulator scaling. saw similar when we enabled heterogeneous tiling last quarter. activation scaling floor gets clipped in tail.

kai: can we reproduce locally with a pinned seed? share run command.

zara: repro: `python run_eval.py --model orion-7b --backend fp8-kernel --tiling hetero --seed 42 --max-prefix 2048 --eval-set longprefix-sample`

log-bot: canary metrics uploaded — token divergence (top-5 mismatch vs fp16) increased by 0.8% overall, but 2.6% on longprefix. no NaNs.

mohit: interesting — is the quantization using per-channel scale or global scale?

ashley: FP8 path uses per-tensor scale with auto-scale heuristic. switching to per-channel is a config we can try.

zara: also saw that AWQ/GPTQ modes didn't show the same magnitude of regression (AWQ ~ -0.6pts).

eva: that suggests the issue is kernel-level accumulation/tiling rather than quant static rounding.

ashley: short mitigation experiment: patch kernel to clamp accumulator pre-activation and reduce tile stride from 128->96. results:

```
longprefix  fp8-kernel+clamp   quality_delta
baseline_fp16 0.734            n/a
fp8-original  0.710            -2.4pts
fp8-clamp      0.725            -0.9pts
latency hit ~+3%
```

ashley: perf hit small, quality mostly recovered. needs more perf regression testing.

mohit: sound plan. curious if per-channel quant + clamp gives full recovery without perf hit. can you run a quick A/B with per-channel scale?

ashley: on it. launching ab job now (job id: ab-171860-07).

infra-bot: deployed kernel patch to canary cluster cny-2024-07-16-12 (nodetype: h100-l40s-canary). monitoring 30m.

log-bot: ab-171860-07 started. baseline shards: 6.

zara: if per-channel + clamp still bad, rollback plan: revert to fp16 kernel on canary and promote AWQ fallback for longprefix traffic. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quant-canary-rollback

kai: small repro note — set `KV_WARMUP=on` to see fuller effect; otherwise tail behavior is masked.

mohit: good catch. can we add a guard in routing: route requests with prefix_len>1024 to fp16/AWQ until kernel is stable?

ashley: yes we can add a soft-routing rule with weight to avoid full rollback. I'll open a PR to routing config and add to the canary policy.

zara: thanks all. action items:
- ashley: finish per-channel ab + post numbers (eta 90m)
- mohit: prepare routing rule PR + test harness (eta 3h)
- eva/kai: add a small unit test that simulates tiled accumulation with long warmup and ensure no floor/clamp surprises (eta EOD)
- infra-bot: keep canary monitoring for 6h and alert on >1% divergence or >2pt rouge drop

zara: tagging for visibility @eng-ml @eng-runtime :thumbsup:
